title: Small wins you can see in-game.
body: Each example teaches one core concept. Copy it into MyFirstAddon.lua, type /reload in-game, and try it out.
reloadBody: Save the file, return to WoW, and type /reload. If something fails, the error message is your best starting point for debugging.

samples.title: Say hello when you log in
samples.description: Create a frame, listen for the login event, and print a friendly message to the chat window.
samples.challenge: Include your character's name using UnitName("player").
samples.code:
local frame = CreateFrame("Frame")
frame:RegisterEvent("PLAYER_LOGIN")

frame:SetScript("OnEvent", function()
  print("Hello, Azeroth!")
end)
samples.skuNote: PLAYER_LOGIN is available on every current SKU.

samples.title: Make your first chat command
samples.description: Register /hello and respond whenever the player types it into chat.
samples.challenge: Accept a name after the command, such as /hello Thrall.
samples.code:
SLASH_MYFIRSTADDON1 = "/hello"

SlashCmdList.MYFIRSTADDON = function(message)
  if message == "" then
    print("Hello from my addon!")
  else
    print("Hello, " .. message .. "!")
  end
end
samples.skuNote: SlashCmdList registration works the same way on every current SKU.

samples.title: Put a button on the screen
samples.description: Create a UI button, position it in the center, and react when it is clicked.
samples.challenge: Make the button draggable and remember its position between sessions.
samples.code:
local button = CreateFrame("Button", nil, UIParent,
  "UIPanelButtonTemplate")
button:SetSize(140, 32)
button:SetPoint("CENTER")
button:SetText("Say hello")

button:SetScript("OnClick", function()
  print("You clicked it!")
end)
samples.skuNote: UIPanelButtonTemplate metrics and default fonts differ on Classic Era and Burning Crusade Anniversary.
